sources.role: resource file (vicerc/vice.ini) format and per-OS locations, FS-device saves
system ROM file names and Directory search path
config-path resolution, vicerc naming and quicksnap filenames (trunk r46226 per contract; cross-checked against the vice-3.10 release tarball)

paths.path: ~/.config/vice/vicerc (GTK builds; SDL2 builds use sdl-vicerc in the same dir), INI-style sections per emulator ([C64], [VIC20], ...) with ResourceName=ResourceValue lines; a legacy ~/.vicerc in $HOME is used when present; -config <file> selects a private config
evidence: docs:vice_6 section 6 intro 'on unix systems the resource file is called vicerc and is stored in the users config directory according to the XDG specification (usually ~/.config/vice/)'

paths.path: ~/.config/vice/vicerc (SDL2 sdl-vicerc; private -joymap <file> may be supplied)
paths.naming: Joystick maps are .vjm text with # comments, !CLEAR and <device> <inputtype> <inputindex> <action> <params>; inputtype 0 axis/1 button/2 hat, action 1 joystick pin mask. Resource bindings are JoyDevice1/JoyDevice2=4+host-device-index

paths.path: In place inside the mounted disk (.d64/.g64/...) and tape (.t64/...) images, or with file-system devices (FSDevice8) directly in a host directory; VICE writes no per-game sidecar save files
paths.naming: Disk/tape saves keep the attached image's own name; FS-device saves are <program>.p00/.prg under FSDevice8Dir (FSDevice8SaveP00=1)
evidence: docs:vice_6.1 example vicerc showing FSDevice8Dir and FSDevice8SaveP00
docs:vice_6 section 6.12.1 'Settings for file system devices'
docs:vice_4 section 4.5 'Using disk and tape images'

paths.path: Snapshots are single complete-machine-state files chosen in the save dialog (no fixed directory); GTK3 quick snapshots default to <machine>.vsf (e.g. C64.vsf) in the config dir ~/.config/vice/, the save dialog proposes vice-snapshot-<yyyymmddHHMMSS>.vsf; -snapshot <file> saves from the command line
paths.naming: Extension forced to .vsf; quicksave/quickload hotkeys M-F11/M-F10 use the <machine>.vsf quicksnap; snapshots are version-bound and must not be used for long-term storage (older modules are rejected on load)
evidence: docs:vice_9 sections 9.1/9.2 (snapshot usage, M-F11/M-F10, module format, version rejection)

paths.path: System ROMs are searched on the Directory path list $XDG_DATA_HOME/vice/<EMU>:$prefix/share/vice/<EMU>:<BOOTPATH>/<EMU> with EMU one of C64, C64DTV, C128, PET, PLUS4, CBM-II, SCPU64, VIC20 (drive ROMs under EMU=DRIVES); gap: the lunchbox DB has no VICE firmware_rules rows
paths.naming: C64/C128/VIC20: kernal, basic, chargen (C128 basic is 32 KiB Basic+Editor); PET uses versioned names (kernal-1/2/4..., basic-1/2/4..., edit-*, characters-1/2...); Plus4 adds c1lo/c1hi/c2lo/c2hi function ROMs; drive DOS ROMs like dos1541-325302-01+901229-05.bin. No canonical checksum is declared for this ROM set by the cited VICE documentation/source
evidence: docs:vice_3 section 3 (Directory default) and 3.1 ROM files list
source:src/sysfile.c sysfile_open() appends the EMU subpath to each Directory entry
db:no firmware_rules rows exist for vice

linux.notes: Lunchbox stages a private -config/-joymap pair (contract session), so the user's own vicerc is never written; native game saves stay in the attached disk/tape images.

paths.path: ~/.var/app/net.sf.VICE/.config/vice/vicerc (the sandbox gives the app its own HOME under ~/.var/app/<id>, so the XDG .config/vice layout lands there; SDL build: sdl-vicerc)
~/.var/app/net.sf.VICE/.config/vice/vicerc (SDL2 sdl-vicerc; native -joymap support is separate)
paths.naming: Same .vjm grammar (#, !CLEAR, device/inputtype/inputindex/action/params) and JoyDevice1/JoyDevice2 resource bindings as native VICE

paths.path: Same as native Linux: writes land inside the mounted disk/tape images or FS-device directories visible to the sandbox
paths.naming: Image saves keep the image's own name; FS-device saves are <program>.p00/.prg

paths.path: Snapshots via the save dialog as on native Linux; quicksnap default is ~/.var/app/net.sf.VICE/.config/vice/<machine>.vsf
paths.naming: <machine>.vsf quicksnap (e.g. C64.vsf); dialog-proposed vice-snapshot-<datetime>.vsf; .vsf extension forced

paths.path: System ROMs inside the sandbox: ~/.var/app/net.sf.VICE/.local/share/vice/<EMU> first (XDG data home under the sandbox HOME), then the installed prefix; gap: the lunchbox DB has no VICE firmware_rules rows
paths.naming: Same per-machine ROM names as native Linux (kernal/basic/chargen etc.); no canonical checksum is declared for this ROM set by the cited VICE documentation/source
evidence: db:no firmware_rules rows exist for vice
